name: Kefrens bars
description: The single-scanline bar trick, several bars deep: every row shows each bar as it was some frames earlier, so the columns snake. Nearer bars are wider, brighter, faster and swing further, so they cross in front of one another at different rates, and every halo is additive so a crossing brightens. Each bar drags a train of ghosts — the afterimage a long-persistence CRT gave this effect for free — over a breathing zoom that never quite repeats.

bars.description: How many bars, spread from nearest to furthest. 1 is the historically accurate version and leaves most of the screen empty.

speed.description: Master rate. Each bar runs at its own fraction of it, so the near ones always outpace the far ones.

lag.description: Phase delay per scanline — the effect itself. Higher coils the column more tightly; at 0 every bar is a straight vertical line.

amplitude.description: How far the nearest bar swings, as a fraction of half the frame. Past 1 the near bars leave the frame at the ends of their travel, which the further ones fill.

ghost.description: Spacing and brightness of the trailing afterimages. 0 collapses them onto the bar and turns them off.

zoom.description: Field of view, on top of a slow breathing zoom the effect does anyway. Below 1 pushes in, so the bars run off the edges and the frame is all motion.
